Classic Survival of the Fittest (2016-2022) was great, but the playerbase died off because 

A - Wildcard stopped updating it
B - Wildcard made it so that its no longer free to play unless you own the base game ARK

Then wildcard announced they were going to resurrect the game, I was very excited. But they lied to their playerbase with misleading trailers. it wasnt a massive update to the classic SOTF, it was THE Survival Of The Fittest, and entirely new game altogether. wildcard got rid of the old game and replaced it with the new one. Its terrible, it strips away every mechanic that made SOTF unique. Theres no farming, Crafting, Levelling, No player v player combat, instead everyone just tames big hoards of dinos and whoever has the most wins every fight. Its like the ship of theseus metaphor, when you take away every single mechanic from Ark SOTF and replace it with something new, is it even ark anymore?

I addressed my concerns with the game to the lead developer of the new SOTF in the Ark discord server, to which she promptly responded by perma-banning me because she was insecure no one liked her game

This isnt an opinion, its a fact. The original SOTF launched in 2016 and it took about a year and a half for the game to die off completely, the new SOTF took 3 months. Just have a look at steam charts

what an absolute disgrace, a year and a half later and im still salty

I’ve had my heart broken several times in my life. 

Once, on Christmas Day 1995, I eagerly ran downstairs and gasped at the sight of what was clearly a crudely but lovingly wrapped skateboard. A skateboard that I had wanted ever since I had seen Marty McFly cruise through the streets of Hi Valley as a stowaway behind an unsuspecting SUV driver. 

A skateboard with a custom deck, with artwork that would cause my fellow skaters to shout "cool". A skateboard whose wheels would send me gliding across the streets as I headed for the nearest half-pipe. A skateboard of majestical proportions.

I grabbed it, and with shaking hands and my heart beating against my chest, I tore that festive wrapper as hard as I could. Through an intricate web of sticky tape, ribbon and ever expanding wrapping paper, I dug through. 

Years later, I wondered if this is what Andy in The Shawshank Redemption must have felt like as he dragged himself through the tunnels. My own redemption was in sight. My prize was near. Finally, the last shred of wrapping fell off to the floor. 

And there it was.. a cheap plastic skateboard from Walmart. With stiff plastic wheels. And a picture of a clown on the deck.

That's what playing ARK the survival of the fittest felt like.

I love Survival of the Fittest and this review will break down what i think are the pros and cons.
PROS:
A battle royale based off Ark is such a neat concept and this does that job somewhat well for the time it was made.
Despite the other reviews, you can get into games, just not official ones. You have to go unofficial.
A good test of skill against some other players.
You get it free with a purchase of Ark. Probably should be free separately though to get more people involved.
CONS:
Abandoned by Wildcard because they probably didn't want to work on it so it is basically a blast from the past with the old Island design and sounds and creatures.
Small playerbase is also an issue as I see between 12-30 people on at one time which means you might have to wait for a match to end to get into another one.
Custom flags you import crash the game unless everytime you go to open SOTF, you delete the saved painting with .last at the end of its name.
CONCLUSION:
I like it but it sure has fallen from grace it once (argueably) had.

This game mode is ARK, but without all of the things that makes ARK great. It doesn't even play well as a stand alone battle royale, which is disappointing as the formula has been close to perfected over the last decade due to all of the competition in the space. It's not like there aren't already battle royal games with building/crafting in them. I don't understand how they could get this so wrong.

Here are just a few of many reasons why I can't recommend SOTF, as much as I love ARK! 

- Finding a server to join a game is anything but intuitive. In fact it's a huge pain. I've spent more time painting my character in empty lobbies than fighting in matches.

- SOTF feels like a mobile phone game with it's overly simplified UI, mechanics and controls. This is supposed to be ARK right? I want the quick bar and inventory from the main game not radial menus.

- There is so much focus on creature combat that you may as well just be a dinosaur.

All in all, the original SOTF was way better than this. All it needed was the current main game UI, matchmaking/lobby and some balance changes to improve the pace of the game. This feels like a gimmick to me. I can't be the only one either. There's barely enough players to start a match. My guess is no PvP players were consulted during the development of this PvP mode. Fingers crossed they fix this. It's worth saving!

The new update has Ruined the game. 
SOTF was a great BR game, it was unique with many ways to play. That was until the December 23 update. The new game is completely different from what it was, hardly even resembling the original SOTF and little to no resemblance to survival evolved. Studio Wild Card decided to take out almost all the features that made the game so great before. Such as removing the crafting and the inventory system as a whole, opting for limited and fast paced game play similar that is more consistent with fortnite than it is with the original game. 

    The new UI is atrocious and over the top with way to much screen clutter. The style of the new UI looks closer to that of a mobile game than it does to the game it is supposedly based on. It has large icons consisting of bright colours with no hot bar for items only armour, and a large map. If you want to look at your inventory system you only get a radial menu that has 8 slots for predetermined items. You cannot switch items for ease of use in this menu. The screen is constantly lit up with pop ups from an enemy looting nearby or losing a dino. With the constant pop ups and over the top UI your screen is blasted with way to much unnecessary information. The devs also decided to switch out the old system for finding a game (which in my opinion was better suited for a BR style gamemode) to the ARK survival evolved server list. Ironically enough the only change to the UI that resembles ark in any way was unnecessary.

    The gameplay is severely worsened. There is no resource gathering, essentially rendering many of the dinosaurs useless. Which is a key element in ARK. You cannot craft weapons or any gear aside from a very limited option via a radial menu which is typically only ammo and grenades. Removing guns forces players into one play style consisting of using the most powerful dinos. there is no point in taming anything other than meta dinos since classic resource gathering dinosaurs are useless due to the devs removing the crafting mechanic. You cannot tame a anklyo and farm metal to get flak armour and guns, you HAVE to tame a damage dealing dino and level them up to fight or you just lose. The low variety of usable weapons limits this even further. The taming system has been "reworked "as well. Another element that made the game stand out removed. Instead of gathering resources, like narcoberries and prime meat to tame a rex, you simply need to kill it and have enough points to tame. which is easy and less rewarding since you take very little damage from Dinos and do a lot more damage to them compared to before. The points are easily gathered by killing trikes and anything that is not a spino or rex with a bow from a green drop. After you tame the rex you will find that the level system has also received a rework. The Dinosaurs no longer have levels and instead have to be leveled up to a certain tier (maxing out at 3) to make them stronger. You cannot chose what to level in your tame or go for a certain build, you just get overall more powerful. The update essentially stripped away anything good about ARK survival evolved, and SOTF turning the game into a fast paced simple mobile game with little depth but at the price of a full game. The Dev team should have made the game free (it was originally but for some reason changed) update the game to match the current state of ARK such as new dinos guns and biomes and reworked the map. OR  they should have just left it alone, better to leave the game dead than to disgrace it like this.

In Survival of the Fittest, players enter the same arena, in the image of the Hunger Games films. The only goal that must be achieved at any cost is to survive. There are many ways to survive. Depending on the mode, you can recruit a team of up to 6 players and become a single tribe. In ARK: Survival of the Fittest, you will be attacked by giant ancient mosquitoes, predatory dinosaurs, spiders and lizards. If you want to hide from them in a pond, then be prepared for piranha bites in the heel. You will freeze, starve, you will be hot, you will break bones dozens of times… And for dessert, a squad of other similar players wants to kill you.
If life in the Survival of the Fittest arena seems like honey to you, then you just didn't wait for the "evolutionary" events. Cataclysms like acid rain, extreme cold or heat occur throughout the game. However, there are also useful events among them: an increase in the speed of domestication or resources are extracted faster.
Up to 72 people can play in the ARK: Survival of the Fittest match at the same time. The developers say that their brainchild will grow into an esports discipline. Well, it could be.

ARK: Survival of the Fittest is a survival arena "esport". It resembles the Hunger Games trilogy, you start falling from the sky into platforms, and from there your only goal is to survive. 

Many people didn't get the "survive" part of it, since it is one of the most quick-paced and hardcore games there is of its kind. The learning curve is extremely steep, with no tutorials nor guides to follow from the developers themselves. Most players quitted and the amount of people that played lowered exponentially, since it wasn't fun for unexperienced players with no learning material.

Another reason why players quitted was the lack of new resources, and the amount of care the developers gave to the game, which was close to nothing. Sure, there were some tournaments in place, but these were won by the same people most of the time, since it is a hard to learn game. 

Today, the lobbies for a match to take place take a long time to start, because of the lack of players. The game is outdated, and tournaments no longer take place. Many people take advantage of the new players and kill them for the additional points which affect their ranks. This game is in the edge of complete extinction or in its way to the renovation of the game, bringing more and more players. This all depends on what the developers decide to do. 

I would recommend playing it, since it is very fun and addictive if you get the hang of it. Remmember, watch youtube videos and guides on how to get better, or you will be one of the thousands that quit for the learning curve. Most of us are hoping for an update in January, but this is up to the developers.
